friday.scored_on: Friday rows in the week model's test split (the model never trained on them)

notes: Suricata 7 with the ET Open rules, run offline on each pcap with HOME_NET set to the victim network (lab 10.10.2.0/24, CIC-IDS2017 192.168.10.0/24) and EXTERNAL_NET any. A flow counts as detected by Suricata when an attack signature (message not starting 'SURICATA ') matched it: same protocol and 5-tuple (either direction; ICMP: same two addresses) with the alert time within 1 s of the flow; each alert is credited to one flow only (the one containing it, else the nearest). Engine events are reported separately. Informational signatures (message starting ET INFO, ET POLICY, GPL ICMP_INFO, GPL INFO or GPL POLICY, or category Not Suspicious Traffic, Misc activity or Potential Corporate Privacy Violation) are counted in 'all attack signatures' and left out of the '_security' figures. The ML model detects a flow when its predicted class is not BENIGN (any attack class, so SYN flood and SQL injection, which are not model classes, can still count); ml_family_recall_* is the stricter same-family measure. 'floor' is the sensor's 0.5 alert floor, 'no_floor' plain argmax. Either = Suricata or ML. Flow-level recall is unfair to Suricata: many ET rules are thresholded (one alert per source per period) and fire on one packet of a scan or flood, so a scan of 1,000 flows can raise a handful of alerts that match only a few flows. 'any_alert' (at least one flow of the label alerted) and the per-session attack-level table are the fairer view of whether the attack was noticed at all. Friday: ML and Suricata are scored only on Friday rows of the week model's test split; the ML side is in-distribution (same day and attack tools as training, and part of the test rows have a feature vector that also occurs in train, see split.friday_identical_to_train), so its recall is optimistic; the lab flows were never in training. Lab: the flows are the attacker's flows only (attack sessions) or all flows (benign session), so the BENIGN rates come from the benign sessions; the repeats of one session are not independent. Suricata sees payloads, the ML model only flow statistics.
